pass_rule: Three fresh-chat runs, each scored with score_forum.py brief --key answer-key-t2.json. Table parses (fail closed). Every item D1 to Q1 has a row of its type whose Point and Quote together match every match pattern, whose Point alone matches every point_match pattern, whose Page is in pages, and whose Quote is on that physical page. Every row's Quote is on its cited page (one miss fails the round). No row without a page. One attendee row per attendee A1 to A4 whose Page is one of that attendee's pages (where the pack states the position) and whose Quote is on it. All three runs must pass.
closed_gaps: Tier-1 latent gaps closed here: (i) an attendee row must cite the page that states that attendee's position, not any pack page; (ii) each item's Point alone must carry the fact (point_match), so a Point that only names the topic while the Quote carries the fact no longer counts. Still open: whether a Point says more than its Quote (only a reader can judge that).
counter_metric: Words of the brief per pack page (60 pages) and rows with no page. Must not rise more than 10% against the previous passing version; the first passing version sets the baseline. Tier-1 reference: 49.3 to 51.5 words per page of a 15-page pack, not comparable.

fact_check.salt_rule: Before the fact-check round, two rows are added to the brief under test: S1 is the C2 quote cited at its printed page (36 instead of physical 39); S2 is an invented quote on page 51. Pass as tier 1: every row's verdict matches the checker, and both salted rows are caught.
